intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cooler morning hours. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and bougatsa. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions. This indoor-friendly market is a perfect alternative on hot or rainy days, offering an authentic taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District
experiences.description: As the sun sets and temperatures cool, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood for a traditional Greek meze dinner. Order a spread of grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), tzatziki, dolmades, and fresh bread paired with local ouzo or tsipouro. Thessaloniki is considered Greece's food capital, and this lively district offers dozens of authentic tavernas with outdoor seating perfect for a breezy evening meal.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Board a small-group catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic Santorini caldera. Swim in the warm Aegean Sea at volcanic hot springs, snorkel over lava formations, and watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from the water. A light Greek dinner with wine is typically included on board. The evening timing avoids the intense midday heat while offering the most spectacular lighting for photos.

experiences.name: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen, ideal for avoiding midday heat or rainy weather. Learn to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). The instructor sources ingredients from local markets and explains the history and health benefits of the Mediterranean diet. You'll enjoy eating everything you cook as a full meal at the end.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka district. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a souvlaki wrap from a street vendor to kick off your Greek food experience.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros or tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the airport or on arrival
meals.dinner: Souvlaki wrap from a street stall in Monastiraki (~€3–4) — try Kostas or Thanasis near the square

day_by_day.notes: Buy an Ath.ena reloadable transit card at the airport Metro station for cheaper rides throughout your Athens stay. Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for travel recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€30) includes several nearby sites valid for 5 days — great value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for local color and cheap souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and ouzeries. Enjoy a budget mezze spread with locals.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery (~€3)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap gyros or a sesame koulouri ring bread from a street cart near the Agora (~€2–3)
meals.dinner: Taverna in Psiri — order shared mezze: tzatziki, horiatiki (Greek salad), grilled bread, and a small carafe of house wine (~€12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — the Acropolis involves uneven marble surfaces. Bring water and sunscreen as temperatures can reach 23°C+. The combined ticket saves significant money if you plan to visit multiple ancient sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis Museum (€10 entry) — one of the world's best archaeological museums with stunning glass-floor views of excavations below. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Parthenon frieze originals and ancient artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to Piraeus port and catch a budget ferry to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour, ~€8–10 each way). Aegina is a perfect day-trip island with beautiful beaches and the famous Temple of Aphaia.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Piraeus by early evening. Head back to Athens and enjoy dinner in the Koukaki neighborhood — a local, less touristy area near the Acropolis.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a café near your hostel (~€4)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a simple psarotaverna (fish tavern) on Aegina's waterfront (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Moussaka or pastitsio at a neighborhood taverna in Koukaki (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance at the Piraeus port or online. Aegina is also famous for its pistachios — buy a small bag from a local vendor as a cheap, delicious snack. This is your first taste of island life!

day_by_day.morning: Use your combined ticket to visit the Roman Agora and Tower of the Winds in Athens. Then explore the Kerameikos archaeological site (also on the combined ticket) — an ancient cemetery and pottery district that most tourists skip, making it peaceful and uncrowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take an afternoon bus from Athens to Cape Sounion (~2 hours, ~€7 from Pedion Areos park bus terminal). Visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff above the Aegean Sea — one of Greece's most dramatic ancient sites.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by bus. Enjoy a quiet evening in the Thissio neighborhood with views of the Acropolis lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and coffee from a local zacharoplasteio (pastry shop) (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic — grab bread, olives, feta, and tomatoes from a local mini-market (~€5) and eat with a view at Sounion
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus and a glass of ouzo at a Thissio café-bar (~€10–12)

day_by_day.notes: The last bus back from Sounion departs around 9:00 PM in summer — confirm the schedule at the terminal. Sunset at the Temple of Poseidon is spectacular and worth timing your visit around.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the early morning bus from Athens to Nafplio (~2.5 hours, ~€14 from KTEL Kifissos terminal). Nafplio is a charming coastal town in the Peloponnese and a perfect budget base. Check into a budget guesthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful old town — stroll along the waterfront promenade, visit the Venetian Bourtzi fortress (small boat taxi ~€5 return), and climb the 999 steps up to the imposing Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Nafplio's narrow old-town streets. Browse the local shops and settle in for a relaxed dinner at a waterfront taverna.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and koulouri at the Athens bus terminal before departure
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or a cheese pie from a local bakery in Nafplio after arrival (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood mezze at a waterfront taverna in Nafplio — try grilled sardines, taramosalata, and village salad (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is widely considered one of Greece's most beautiful towns. Book your budget accommodation in advance as it's popular in June. The Palamidi climb is strenuous — go in the late afternoon when it's cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Epidaurus (~30 min by local bus, ~€3). Visit the ancient Theatre of Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world, famous for its extraordinary acoustics. Also explore the Sanctuary of Asclepius.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, clean pebble beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Free entry, calm waters, and a beautiful setting beneath the Palamidi cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the longest day of the year (summer solstice) with a sunset drink at one of Nafplio's rooftop bars or waterfront cafés. Watch the golden light over the Argolic Gulf.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait and coffee at a café in Nafplio's Syntagma Square (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the local market — olives, bread, local cheese, and fruit (~€5) eaten at Epidaurus
meals.dinner: Grilled lamb chops (paidakia) with roasted potatoes at a local grill house (psistaria) in Nafplio (~€12–14)

day_by_day.notes: June 21 is the summer solstice — the longest day of the year, perfect for maximizing sightseeing hours. Check if any special performances are scheduled at the Epidaurus theatre during your visit — summer festival tickets can be surprisingly affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Nafplio to Athens by bus, then connect to Piraeus port. Take a budget ferry to Hydra island (~2 hours from Piraeus, ~€15–18 each way). Hydra is unique — no cars or motorbikes allowed, only donkeys and boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hydra Town on foot — the beautiful stone mansions, the port, and the narrow alleyways. Hike or take a water taxi (~€5–8) to one of the island's rocky swimming spots like Vlychos or Kamini beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Hydra's car-free port at sunset. Have dinner at a portside taverna before catching the evening ferry back to Piraeus.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Piraeus port before boarding the ferry (~€3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a simple taverna in Hydra Town — ask for the daily catch (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Mezze plate with local wine at a portside restaurant before the return ferry (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Hydra is one of Greece's most atmospheric islands. Water taxis are the main transport around the island — agree on the price before boarding. The ferry schedule back to Piraeus runs until late evening in summer. This is a long travel day so start early.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: From Athens/Piraeus, take a budget ferry to Paros island (~4–5 hours, ~€30–35 on a standard ferry — book in advance for best prices). Paros is a beautiful Cycladic island with excellent beaches and a lively but affordable atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Parikia (Paros Town), check into a budget room or hostel. Explore the charming whitewashed old town, visit the impressive Panagia Ekatontapiliani (Church of 100 Doors) — free entry — and stroll along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Parikia's lively evening scene. The main street (Market Street) is lined with affordable tavernas, bars, and local shops. Enjoy a relaxed first evening on the island.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tiropita at a bakery near Piraeus port before boarding (~€3)
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry — bring your own food from Athens to save money, or buy a simple sandwich on board
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish or a hearty Greek salad with bread at a budget taverna in Parikia old town (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Paros ferry well in advance for June travel — ferries fill up quickly in peak season. Consider a high-speed ferry if budget allows (saves 2+ hours). Paros will be your base for the next 3 nights.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV in Parikia (~€20–25/day) to explore the island independently. Head to Naoussa — a picturesque fishing village in the north with a beautiful Venetian harbor. Explore the village and the ruins of the Venetian castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Naoussa, head to Kolymbithres beach — famous for its unique granite rock formations and crystal-clear turquoise water. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. Nearby Santa Maria beach is also excellent and less crowded.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Parikia. Enjoy a sunset walk along the waterfront and dinner at a local taverna. Try fresh seafood — Paros is known for excellent fish.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a fresh cheese pie from a Parikia bakery (~€3)
meals.lunch: Grilled octopus and a cold Mythos beer at a simple café in Naoussa (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Grilled sea bream (tsipoura) with lemon and olive oil at a Parikia taverna (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Kolymbithres is one of the most photographed beaches in the Cyclades — arrive before noon to secure a good spot. The scooter rental gives you freedom to explore at your own pace and is very cost-effective for a full day of island exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Take the short ferry from Paros to Antiparos (~15 min, ~€1.50) — a tiny, tranquil island perfect for a relaxed morning. Explore the small village and the medieval Venetian castle in the center of town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at one of Antiparos's beautiful beaches — Sifneikos or Glyfa are excellent, uncrowded options with clear water. This is pure, unspoiled Greek island life at its best.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Paros. Enjoy your last evening on Paros with a farewell dinner. Try local Parian wine — the island has a small but quality wine tradition.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt with local thyme honey and walnuts at a café in Parikia (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Simple grilled fish or a mezze plate at a beachside taverna on Antiparos (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Lamb stifado (slow-cooked stew) with crusty bread and local wine at a Parikia taverna (~€12–14)

day_by_day.notes: Antiparos is a wonderful hidden gem — far less crowded than Paros and Mykonos. The cave of Antiparos (a famous stalactite cave) is worth visiting if you have extra time in the morning. Bring cash as some small establishments on Antiparos don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry from Paros to Santorini (~2–3 hours, ~€20–30). Arrive in Santorini and check into a budget hostel or guesthouse in Fira or Perissa (Perissa is cheaper and right on a black sand beach).
day_by_day.afternoon: If staying in Perissa, spend the afternoon at Perissa Black Sand Beach — one of Santorini's best and most accessible beaches. The dramatic black volcanic sand and clear blue water are stunning. Beach access is free.
day_by_day.evening: Take the local bus (~€1.80) from Perissa to Fira — Santorini's main town. Walk along the caldera edge at sunset for the famous Santorini views without paying Oia prices. Explore Fira's winding streets.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Paros port before the ferry (~€3)
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or grab a gyros near the Santorini port on arrival (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Budget taverna in Fira — try tomatokeftedes (Santorini tomato fritters) and fava dip, local specialties (~€10–12)

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is the most expensive Greek island — staying in Perissa or Kamari instead of Oia or Fira saves significant money. The local bus network is excellent and very cheap, connecting all major villages and beaches. Avoid overpriced caldera-view restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Oia village (~45 min, €1.80) in the morning before the crowds arrive. Explore the iconic blue-domed churches, the Venetian castle ruins, and the narrow alleyways. The morning light is beautiful and the village is far less crowded than at sunset.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by bus to the Akrotiri area. Visit the Akrotiri Archaeological Site (~€12) — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age city buried by a volcanic eruption, often called the 'Minoan Pompeii.' Afterward, relax at Red Beach nearby — a dramatic beach with towering red volcanic cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your base. Enjoy a final Santorini sunset from a free viewpoint — the Skaros Rock near Imerovigli or the Fira caldera path offer stunning views without the Oia crowds. Celebrate with a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local cherry tomatoes, and feta from a Perissa mini-market — eat on the beach (~€4)
meals.lunch: Simple gyros or souvlaki from a grill near Akrotiri (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Grilled fresh fish and a carafe of local Assyrtiko white wine at a Perissa taverna — Santorini's Assyrtiko is world-class (~€14–16)

day_by_day.notes: Santorini's Assyrtiko white wine is a must-try — it's produced locally and pairs perfectly with seafood. Red Beach requires a short rocky walk — wear sturdy sandals. Book your return ferry or flight from Santorini to Athens in advance to secure the best budget prices.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Santorini. Take one last swim at Perissa or Kamari beach. Pack up and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — local thyme honey, Santorini capers, and small ceramic pieces make affordable, authentic gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Santorini port (Athinios) for your ferry or to the airport for your return flight to Athens or directly home. If you have time in Athens before your departure, grab one last souvlaki and a Greek coffee in Monastiraki.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — fly home with incredible memories of 13 days of Greek beaches, ancient history, and delicious local food on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a Perissa café — eggs, local cheese, olives, tomatoes, and coffee (~€6–8) as a final treat
meals.lunch: Last gyros wrap or a cheese pie from a bakery near the port (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight — or a final souvlaki in Athens if connecting through (~€4–5)

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding international flights): approximately €600–800 per person, covering budget accommodation (~€25–35/night), local transport, ferry tickets, entrance fees, and meals. Greece rewards travelers who eat where locals eat, use public buses, and choose standard ferries over high-speed options. Kalό taxídi — safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens (~40 min, €9). Check into your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle stroll around Monastiraki Square to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Monastiraki Flea Market (open late) and enjoy your first views of the illuminated Acropolis. Head to Psiri neighborhood for dinner at a traditional taverna.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a coffee and tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki Square (€3–5) after settling in
meals.dinner: Taverna in Psiri neighborhood — try grilled octopus, tzatziki, and a Greek salad with local house wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage light for the metro ride. Book accommodation in Monastiraki or Koukaki for easy access to central Athens sights.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis (open from 8:00 AM) before the crowds and heat build up. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€20) includes entry to several other ancient sites. Arrive by 8:00–8:30 AM for the best experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum (€10 entry) at the base of the hill — world-class exhibits with original friezes and sculptures. Afterward, explore the Ancient Agora of Athens, the old marketplace where Socrates once walked (included in combined ticket).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Thissio or Monastiraki rooftop bars for sunset cocktails with Acropolis views. Then dinner in the lively Plaka neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, freddo espresso (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the Acropolis Museum — spanakopita, horiatiki salad, and fresh lemonade (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Plaka — moussaka, lamb chops (paidakia), and local Assyrtiko white wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen. The Acropolis involves significant uphill walking on uneven marble surfaces. Arrive early to beat both crowds and heat (23°C average high).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Archaeological Museum (€12 entry) — one of the world's greatest collections of ancient Greek artifacts, including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tram or bus to the Athens Riviera. Spend the afternoon at Vouliagmeni Lake or Asteras Beach in Glyfada — clean, organized beaches about 25 km from central Athens. Swim in the clear Aegean waters (entry €8–15 for organized beaches).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens and explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood. Browse boutiques and enjoy aperitifs at a rooftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Neighborhood bakery near your hotel — koulouri (sesame bread ring), coffee, and fresh orange juice (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Glyfada — fresh grilled fish, calamari, and Greek salad with a cold Mythos beer (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Modern Greek cuisine restaurant in Kolonaki — creative mezedes and grilled sea bream (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera beaches are easily accessible by tram from Syntagma Square. Bring a beach bag, towel, and reef-safe sunscreen. June weather is ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning flight or ferry to Santorini. Flights from Athens to Santorini take ~45 min (book in advance, €50–90). Alternatively, take a high-speed ferry from Piraeus (~5 hours, €40–60). Arrive and check into a mid-range hotel in Fira or Firostefani with caldera views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fira town — the island's capital. Walk the caldera-edge path from Fira to Firostefani and Imerovigli (about 3 km, stunning views). Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (€6) to learn about the Minoan civilization buried by the volcanic eruption.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from Imerovigli or the less-crowded Skaros Rock viewpoint (avoid the overly touristy Oia crowds if you prefer a quieter experience). Dinner in Fira.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Athens airport or on the ferry
meals.lunch: Gyros or souvlaki from a local spot in Fira after arriving and settling in (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Caldera-view restaurant in Fira — fresh Santorinian fava (yellow split pea dip), white eggplant salad, and grilled local fish (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book flights or ferry tickets well in advance for June travel. Mid-range hotels in Fira or Firostefani offer caldera views at more reasonable prices than Oia. The caldera walk is moderately strenuous.

day_by_day.morning: Rent an ATV or scooter (€20–30/day) and head to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the south coast — famous for their dramatic black volcanic sand. Swim and relax in the clear blue water. The contrast of black sand and turquoise sea is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive up to Ancient Akrotiri — the remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption around 1600 BC (€12 entry). Often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Afterward, visit the Red Beach nearby for a short swim — accessible by a 10-minute walk over volcanic rocks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira and enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere. Browse the local shops for Santorinian products — local wine, capers, and fava. Dinner at a local restaurant away from the main tourist strip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café in Fira — Greek yogurt parfait, eggs, and coffee (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Beach bar at Perissa — fresh seafood pasta, Greek salad, and cold drinks (€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Local taverna in Fira's back streets — Santorinian tomato fritters (tomatokeftedes), grilled lamb, and local Assyrtiko wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the Akrotiri site and Red Beach walk. The Red Beach path involves scrambling over volcanic rocks — take care. Santorinian Assyrtiko wine is world-class and very affordable locally.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat tour of the Santorini caldera (€25–40 per person). Visit the active volcanic island of Nea Kameni, hike to the crater, and swim in the warm sulfuric hot springs at Palea Kameni. Most tours depart from Fira's old port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the picturesque village of Oia in the afternoon (less crowded than sunset time). Explore the narrow blue-domed streets, browse art galleries, and enjoy the iconic architecture. Walk the 10 km caldera path from Fira to Oia (allow 3–4 hours) or take a bus (€1.80).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Oia for the legendary sunset — arrive at least 1 hour early to secure a good viewpoint. The sunset from Oia's castle ruins is one of the most spectacular in the world. Dinner in Oia before returning to Fira.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat tour — pastry and coffee from a Fira bakery (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack on the boat tour, or a quick bite in Oia — fresh seafood mezedes (€15–20)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Oia — splurge slightly for the atmosphere: lobster pasta or fresh catch of the day with local wine (€35–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the caldera boat tour the day before. The Fira-to-Oia caldera walk is one of Greece's most scenic hikes — bring water, sunscreen, and a hat. Buses between Fira and Oia run frequently (€1.80).

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Santorini to Crete (Heraklion port) — high-speed ferry takes ~2 hours (€35–55). Depart early morning to maximize your day. Check into a mid-range hotel in Heraklion or the charming old town of Chania (if you prefer, take a bus west to Chania, ~2.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: If staying in Heraklion: Visit the Palace of Knossos (€15) — the legendary Minoan palace and Europe's oldest city, dating back 4,000 years. Fascinating labyrinthine ruins with colorful frescoes. If you've traveled to Chania: Explore the stunning Venetian harbor and old town.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's lively market street (1866 Street) for local products — Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, and raki. Dinner in the old town near the Morosini Fountain.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Santorini port café before the ferry (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Traditional Cretan lunch near Knossos — dakos (barley rusk with tomato and feta), stuffed vine leaves, and local beer (€12–18)
meals.dinner: Cretan taverna in Heraklion old town — slow-cooked lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and a carafe of local Cretan wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Crete is Greece's largest island with a distinct culinary identity — Cretan cuisine is considered among the healthiest in the world. Book ferry tickets in advance for June. Consider renting a car in Crete for maximum flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus west to the Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest gorges (16 km). The hike takes 4–6 hours and descends from the White Mountains to the Libyan Sea. Entry €5. Start early (buses from Chania depart ~6:30–7:30 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Samaria Gorge hike and emerge at the village of Agia Roumeli on the Libyan Sea. Reward yourself with a swim in the crystal-clear water and a cold drink at a beachside café. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (€15, ~1 hour), then bus back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Chania by early evening. Explore the magical Venetian harbor at dusk — the lighthouse, the old mosque, and the colorful waterfront. Dinner along the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before the bus — energy-rich food: bread, cheese, and fruit (pack snacks for the hike)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the gorge — sandwiches, nuts, and plenty of water. Or eat at the Agia Roumeli taverna at the end (fresh fish, €15–20)
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant at Chania's Venetian harbor — fresh Cretan seafood, grilled octopus, and local Vidiano white wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge is strenuous — wear proper hiking shoes, bring 2+ liters of water, sunscreen, and snacks. The gorge is closed in bad weather. Check conditions the day before. This is a full-day excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before dawn and drive ~1.5 hours from Chania to Elafonissi Beach in southwest Crete. Arrive at sunrise for the 'Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach' experience — the famous pink-sand beach with its shallow turquoise lagoon is magical at this hour, virtually empty and bathed in golden light. Wade through the shallow lagoon to the small island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at Elafonissi — swim, snorkel, and explore the pink-tinged sand (the color comes from crushed coral and shells). The water is exceptionally clear and shallow, making it ideal for swimming. Head back toward Chania in the early afternoon, stopping at the scenic Topolia Gorge or the village of Elos for a break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania. Visit the covered market (Agora) for local shopping. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the old town — explore the narrow Venetian streets, visit a local raki bar (rakadiko) for complimentary raki and mezedes.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast to eat at the beach at sunrise — yogurt, fruit, and coffee in a thermos
meals.lunch: Beach taverna near Elafonissi — fresh grilled fish, Cretan salad, and cold drinks (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Rakadiko (raki bar) in Chania old town — complimentary raki with small mezedes plates, then a proper dinner at a nearby taverna: lamb with artichokes, Cretan cheeses (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is best visited early — it gets very crowded by mid-morning in June. The drive from Chania is scenic but involves mountain roads. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the fragile ecosystem. Parking is available (€3–5).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Chania's old town in depth — visit the Archaeological Museum of Chania (housed in a Venetian church, €4), the Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Collection, and the historic lighthouse. Walk the full length of the Venetian harbor walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a bus to Balos Lagoon (alternatively, take a boat tour from Kissamos port, ~€20 round trip). Balos is one of Greece's most photographed beaches — a stunning lagoon with white sand and turquoise water where three seas meet. The hike down from the parking area takes ~20 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for your final evening on the island. Enjoy a leisurely dinner and pick up last-minute Cretan souvenirs — olive oil soap, thyme honey, and local cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Café in Chania old town — Cretan breakfast with local cheeses, olives, honey, and rusks (€10–14)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Balos or pack a picnic — sandwiches, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Farewell Cretan dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant — slow-roasted goat (antikristo), wild greens, and aged graviera cheese with local wine (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Balos can also be reached by 4WD vehicle via a rough dirt road (free) or by boat from Kissamos. The boat option is more comfortable and scenic. Book the boat in advance in June.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Chania (CHQ) or Heraklion (HER) back to Athens (~45 min, €40–80). Check into a hotel near Syntagma or the Plaka for your final days. Visit the Benaki Museum (€9) — Greece's premier cultural history museum with an extraordinary collection spanning 5,000 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood and the National Garden — a peaceful green oasis in the heart of Athens. Visit the Panathenaic Stadium (Kallimarmaro) — the original Olympic stadium built entirely of white marble, used in the 1896 Olympics (€5 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your penultimate evening in Athens. Head to the lively Exarchia or Metaxourgeio neighborhoods for a more authentic, local Athens experience — street art, independent cafés, and neighborhood tavernas.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Chania airport or hotel before the flight
meals.lunch: Café near the Benaki Museum — light Greek lunch: salad, grilled vegetables, and fresh bread (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Neighborhood taverna in Exarchia — home-style Greek cooking: stuffed peppers, pastitsio (Greek lasagna), and local wine (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Benaki Museum also has an excellent rooftop café with Acropolis views. The Panathenaic Stadium allows visitors to run a lap on the track — a memorable experience for sports enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Cape Sounion (1.5 hours from Athens by KTEL bus, €7 each way) — visit the dramatic Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60 meters above the Aegean Sea (€10 entry). Lord Byron carved his name into one of the columns. The views are breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Athens and visit the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — Athens' vibrant covered market with fish, meat, spices, and produce stalls. A feast for the senses. Browse the surrounding streets for olives, nuts, and local delicacies to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore somewhere new. Consider a food tour of Athens (€45–65 per person) to sample multiple local specialties in one evening, or simply enjoy a long, leisurely Greek dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or neighborhood café — eggs, feta, tomatoes, and Greek coffee (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a taverna near Cape Sounion — fresh catch, grilled sardines, and a cold Alfa beer overlooking the sea (€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner at a well-regarded Athens restaurant — creative modern Greek cuisine with local seasonal ingredients and natural Greek wines (€35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus to Cape Sounion departs from the Pedion Areos park bus stop. The coastal route (recommended) passes several beaches. Sunset at Cape Sounion is spectacular — consider timing your visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a slow breakfast and last coffee at a neighborhood café. Do any remaining souvenir shopping in Monastiraki or the Plaka. Pick up Greek products to bring home: olive oil, mountain tea, mastiha liqueur, and local honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit any remaining sights — the Roman Agora and Tower of the Winds (included in combined ticket), Hadrian's Arch, or simply sit at a café and people-watch. Check out of your hotel and head to Athens International Airport (Metro Line 3 from Syntagma, ~40 min, €9).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Greek beaches, ancient history, and unforgettable food.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final Greek breakfast — bougatsa (custard or cheese-filled pastry), Greek coffee, and fresh juice at a traditional café (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Monastiraki — souvlaki, tzatziki, and pita one last time (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Athens airport. The Metro is the most reliable way to reach the airport. Keep some euros for last-minute purchases. Kalo taxidi — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cooler morning hours. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and bougatsa. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions. This indoor-friendly market is a perfect alternative on hot or rainy days, offering an authentic taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District
experiences.description: As the sun sets and temperatures cool, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood for a traditional Greek meze dinner. Order a spread of grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), tzatziki, dolmades, and fresh bread paired with local ouzo or tsipouro. Thessaloniki is considered Greece's food capital, and this lively district offers dozens of authentic tavernas with outdoor seating perfect for a breezy evening meal.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Board a small-group catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic Santorini caldera. Swim in the warm Aegean Sea at volcanic hot springs, snorkel over lava formations, and watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from the water. A light Greek dinner with wine is typically included on board. The evening timing avoids the intense midday heat while offering the most spectacular lighting for photos.

experiences.name: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen, ideal for avoiding midday heat or rainy weather. Learn to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). The instructor sources ingredients from local markets and explains the history and health benefits of the Mediterranean diet. You'll enjoy eating everything you cook as a full meal at the end.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your 5-star hotel in central Athens (Syntagma/Kolonaki area). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity in your suite.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll through the Plaka neighborhood at dusk — the old town beneath the Acropolis glows beautifully in the early evening light. Browse boutique shops and soak in the atmosphere before dinner.

meals.breakfast: On board the flight
meals.lunch: On board the flight or at the airport upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside (Michelin-starred, modern Greek seafood cuisine) in Mikrolimano, Piraeus — a short private transfer from central Athens. Indulge in tasting menus featuring fresh Aegean catch paired with premium Greek wines.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with your hotel concierge. Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for jet lag recovery and smooth arrival. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings with the concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — Head to the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cool morning hours. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, cured meats, spices, olives, and local cheeses. Sample traditional Greek street foods including koulouri, loukoumades, and fresh-cut charcuterie with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum (one of Europe's finest archaeological museums) for an air-conditioned, in-depth exploration of ancient Athenian artifacts. Follow with a private guided tour of the Acropolis itself and the Parthenon, timed to avoid peak midday heat. Enjoy panoramic views over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Grande Bretagne overlooking Syntagma Square and the Acropolis. Then proceed to dinner at a premium restaurant in Kolonaki.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at your 5-star hotel
meals.lunch: Traditional taverna lunch in Monastiraki — try grilled octopus, dakos salad, and fresh tzatziki at a curated local spot recommended by your guide
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spondi (two Michelin stars) in Pangrati — exquisite French-Mediterranean cuisine with an exceptional Greek wine list in a romantic garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the Acropolis timed-entry tickets in advance to avoid queues. The food tour typically runs 3–4 hours and is best started by 9:00 AM before the heat builds. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Ancient Agora of Athens and the Temple of Hephaestus — one of the best-preserved ancient Greek temples. Explore the Stoa of Attalos museum with a private archaeologist guide for a deeply immersive historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens' upscale Glyfada Riviera by private car. Spend the afternoon at a premium beach club on the Athens Riviera (such as Astir Beach or Yabanaki) — enjoy crystal-clear waters, a private sunbed, and attentive beach service. The water temperature in June is perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Athens. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Kolonaki district — browse high-end boutiques and galleries before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the beach club restaurant — fresh seafood salads, grilled fish, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hytra (Michelin-starred) in Onassis Cultural Centre — innovative modern Greek cuisine with stunning presentation and a curated natural wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera beach clubs require reservations for sunbeds in peak season — book ahead. Private car hire for the day is recommended for flexibility between the Agora and Glyfada.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens for Santorini via a short domestic flight (approximately 45 minutes) or a high-speed ferry from Piraeus. Check into a luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli with a private plunge pool and caldera views. Settle in and enjoy a mid-morning swim in your private pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — wander through whitewashed alleyways, visit the Maritime Museum, browse art galleries, and discover artisan jewelry boutiques. Stop for a refreshing frappe or fresh-squeezed juice at a cliffside café.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around the Santorini Caldera — board a small-group luxury catamaran in the late afternoon. Sail around the volcanic caldera, swim in the hot springs, snorkel in clear Aegean waters, and enjoy a BBQ dinner and open bar on board as the sun melts into the sea.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or en route to the airport/port
meals.lunch: Lunch at Metaxy Mas in Exo Gonia — a beloved local taverna known for exceptional Santorinian cuisine including fava, white eggplant, and fresh tomato fritters
meals.dinner: BBQ dinner and drinks included on the catamaran cruise; supplement with a nightcap at your hotel's cliffside bar

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran cruise well in advance — small-group luxury options fill up quickly in June. Opt for a hotel in Oia or Imerovigli for the most dramatic caldera views. Bring a light layer for the boat as sea breezes can be cool after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a private sunrise yoga session on your hotel terrace overlooking the caldera. Follow with a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then take a private guided hike along the Fira-to-Oia trail (approximately 10 km) — one of the most scenic coastal walks in the Mediterranean, with sweeping caldera views throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Fira and explore the capital of Santorini. Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera to see artifacts from the ancient Akrotiri civilization. Spend time at the Archaeological Site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age settlement often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.'
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for a private sunset dinner at one of the world's most celebrated sunset viewpoints. Enjoy cocktails on your hotel terrace as the sky turns gold and crimson over the caldera.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at your cave hotel with caldera views
meals.lunch: Lunch at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos — a landmark of Santorinian gastronomy, celebrating local ingredients like Assyrtiko wine, capers, and cherry tomatoes
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant in Oia (part of Andronis Luxury Suites) — refined Mediterranean cuisine with unparalleled caldera and sunset views; reserve the best terrace table

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia hike takes 3–4 hours at a leisurely pace. Start by 7:30 AM to avoid midday heat. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and sturdy shoes. Arrange a private transfer back from Fira to Oia after the afternoon museum visit.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at Perissa or Perivolos Beach on Santorini's southeastern coast — dramatic black volcanic sand beaches with clear blue water. Enjoy a private sunbed at a premium beach club with full service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient site of Ancient Thera on the ridge above Perissa — a fascinating Hellenistic and Roman city with sweeping views of both sides of the island. Return to the hotel for a late afternoon rest and spa treatment (book the hotel spa in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Santorini before tomorrow's departure. Enjoy a final evening stroll through Oia's lantern-lit alleyways.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachfront restaurant at Perivolos — grilled whole fish, sea urchin, and chilled Assyrtiko white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ambrosia Restaurant in Oia — elegant cliffside dining with panoramic caldera views, exceptional Greek cuisine, and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book your spa treatment at least 24 hours in advance. Ancient Thera is accessible by a steep road — arrange a taxi or ATV rental. Confirm your ferry or flight to Crete for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning ferry or short flight from Santorini to Heraklion, Crete (ferry approximately 2 hours by high-speed; flight 40 minutes). Check into a luxury boutique hotel in Heraklion or a 5-star resort on the nearby coast. Freshen up and head to the world-class Heraklion Archaeological Museum — home to the finest collection of Minoan art and artifacts in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Bronze Age palace of the Minoan civilization, associated with the myth of the Minotaur and the Labyrinth. Explore with a private expert guide for a rich, immersive experience. Return to the hotel for a refreshing swim and rest during the warmest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's vibrant old town — walk along the Venetian harbor, admire the Koules Fortress, and browse the Lion Square (Morosini Fountain) area.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the Santorini hotel or on the ferry
meals.lunch: Traditional Cretan lunch at Peskesi Restaurant in Heraklion — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant dedicated to authentic Cretan heritage cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Herbs' Garden Restaurant at Lato Boutique Hotel — rooftop dining with views of the Koules Fortress and harbor, featuring refined Cretan cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Knossos is best visited in the morning or late afternoon to avoid peak heat and crowds. A private guide significantly enhances the experience. Book in advance. The Heraklion Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays — adjust if needed by visiting Knossos first.

day_by_day.morning: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion — Join a hands-on Cretan cooking class in a traditional kitchen. Learn to prepare iconic dishes such as dakos, spanakopita, lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades. Discover the secrets of Cretan olive oil, herbs, and the Mediterranean diet from a local chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive west along Crete's northern coast to the charming Venetian harbor town of Rethymno (approximately 1.5 hours by private car). Explore the beautifully preserved old town, the Venetian Fortezza fortress, and the Rimondi Fountain. Browse artisan shops in the narrow alleyways.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of Rethymno's harbor front as fishing boats return and restaurants light up for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the morning cooking class — a delicious and personal Cretan feast
meals.dinner: Dinner at Avli Restaurant in Rethymno — one of Crete's most acclaimed restaurants, set in a romantic Venetian courtyard garden with exceptional local cuisine and an extensive Cretan wine list

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours including the meal. Arrange a private driver for the Rethymno excursion for comfort and flexibility. Consider staying overnight in Rethymno at a boutique luxury hotel to avoid the return drive.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and depart for the legendary Elafonissi Beach on Crete's southwestern tip (approximately 1.5–2 hours from Rethymno by private car). Arrive at sunrise for the Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach — experience the famous pink-sand beach and shallow turquoise lagoon in near-total solitude before the day-trippers arrive. Wade through the warm, crystal-clear shallows and swim in the lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the late morning and early afternoon enjoying Elafonissi's extraordinary beauty — snorkel, sunbathe on the pink sand, and explore the small island accessible by wading. Begin the return journey to your Crete base in the early afternoon, stopping at a traditional village kafeneion for refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Heraklion or your Cretan resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a sunset swim at your hotel pool or private beach.

meals.breakfast: Pack a gourmet picnic breakfast from your hotel to enjoy on the beach at sunrise — fresh pastries, local honey, yogurt, and fruit
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a local taverna near Elafonissi or in the nearby village of Kissamos on the return journey
meals.dinner: Dinner at Erganos Restaurant in Heraklion — a beloved institution for authentic, home-style Cretan cuisine in a warm, rustic setting

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is approximately 76 km from Rethymno and 76 km from Heraklion — a private driver is essential. Depart by 5:30–6:00 AM to arrive at sunrise. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water, and a hat. The beach has very limited facilities early in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Crete for Thessaloniki via a short domestic flight (approximately 1 hour). Check into a luxury hotel in Thessaloniki's city center (Ladadika or Aristotelous Square area). Begin exploring Greece's vibrant second city — visit the iconic White Tower on the waterfront promenade and enjoy views across the Thermaic Gulf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Thessaloniki's remarkable Byzantine heritage — visit the UNESCO-listed Rotunda (Galerius), the Arch of Galerius (Kamara), and the stunning Hagia Sophia of Thessaloniki. Browse the upscale Tsimiski Street for luxury shopping. Visit the Museum of Byzantine Culture — one of the finest Byzantine art museums in the world.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District — As the sun sets, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood (the former oil merchants' quarter) for a traditional Greek meze experience. Enjoy multiple small plates of local specialties — bougatsa, trigona, grilled meats, seafood, and local cheeses — paired with ouzo or tsipouro.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the Crete hotel or at Heraklion Airport
meals.lunch: Lunch at Myrsini Restaurant in Thessaloniki — a refined modern Greek restaurant celebrating northern Greek and Macedonian cuisine
meals.dinner: Premium meze dinner at Extravaganza or Aristotelous Square area restaurants in Ladadika — order a full spread of Thessaloniki specialties including loukaniko, taramosalata, grilled halloumi, and fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki is renowned as Greece's food capital — embrace the local culture of sharing many small dishes. The Ladadika district is best experienced in the evening when it truly comes alive. Book a table at a well-regarded meze restaurant in advance for peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the extraordinary Thessaloniki Archaeological Museum — home to priceless treasures from the royal tombs of Vergina, including the gold larnax (burial chest) of Philip II of Macedon, father of Alexander the Great. A private guide brings this golden age of Macedonia to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day excursion to Vergina (ancient Aigai) — approximately 1.5 hours by private car. Visit the Royal Tombs of Vergina, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the underground museum built within the Great Tumulus. See the actual tomb of Philip II and extraordinary Macedonian gold artifacts in situ. Return to Thessaloniki in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along Thessaloniki's famous waterfront promenade (Nikis Avenue) — a beloved local ritual. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar with panoramic views of the Thermaic Gulf and Mount Olympus on the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Indulge in Thessaloniki's famous breakfast culture — fresh bougatsa (warm custard or cheese phyllo pastry) from a legendary local bougatsa shop such as Bougatsa Bantis or Giannis
meals.lunch: Lunch in Vergina at a local taverna — simple, hearty northern Greek cuisine with grilled meats and local wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Clochard Restaurant in Thessaloniki — an elegant, intimate restaurant with a sophisticated menu of modern Greek and Mediterranean cuisine and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Vergina museum is underground and maintains a cool temperature year-round — bring a light layer. Photography restrictions apply inside the tombs. The round trip with time at the site takes approximately 4–5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Ano Poli (Upper Town) of Thessaloniki — a beautifully preserved Ottoman-era neighborhood with Byzantine walls, wooden-balconied houses, and stunning views over the city and gulf. Visit the Heptapyrgion fortress and the charming neighborhood churches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Excursion to the Chalkidiki Peninsula (approximately 1 hour by private car) — Chalkidiki's three 'fingers' offer some of northern Greece's most beautiful beaches. Head to Sithonia (the middle finger) for pristine, pine-fringed beaches with turquoise water. Spend the afternoon at a premium beach club at Porto Carras or Vourvourou.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Thessaloniki for a final evening in the city. Explore the vibrant Valaoritou district — Thessaloniki's creative and nightlife hub — for cocktails at a sophisticated bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachfront taverna in Sithonia — grilled sea bream, shrimp saganaki, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Zythos Restaurant near the White Tower — a Thessaloniki institution beloved for its exceptional meze, craft beers, and warm atmosphere; order the grilled octopus and the city's famous spicy sausages

day_by_day.notes: Chalkidiki beaches are stunning but can be busy on summer Saturdays — depart early. The drive to Sithonia's best beaches (e.g., Kavourotrypes) takes about 1.5 hours. A private car is essential. Consider a sunset swim before heading back to the city.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thessaloniki — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last stroll along the waterfront. Visit the Modiano and Kapani covered markets for a final taste of Thessaloniki's extraordinary food culture — pick up premium local products to take home: Macedonian honey, saffron from Kozani, Chalkidiki olives, and local spirits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final lunch in the city. Transfer to Thessaloniki Macedonia International Airport (SKG) for your return flight. Allow ample time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Thessaloniki. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the beaches, flavors, history, and culture of Greece — from Athens to Santorini, Crete, and Thessaloniki.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent hotel breakfast — savor it slowly
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Ouzeri Tsinari in the Ano Poli neighborhood — a charming, authentic ouzeri with spectacular city views and classic northern Greek meze
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the destination airport

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the city center by private car. Confirm your return flight details and arrange a private airport transfer the evening before. Pack any purchased food items in checked luggage per airline regulations. Keep a small carry-on bag with essentials for the journey home.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
